teams.synopsis: The most wins in PFFL history, and Freiermuth/Likely already erased the Mark Andrews concern.
teams.blurb: The biggest question surrounding this team a week ago was how it'd handle the loss of <mark class="hl-player">Mark Andrews</mark>, and needless to say, <mark class="hl-player">Freiermuth</mark> and/or <mark class="hl-player">Likely</mark> answered that question and will give this team a good chance at winning in the playoffs. Ethan's team didn't put up the most points in Week 12, but with the most wins by a team in PFFL history, this team remained atop the rankings.

teams.synopsis: The point differential edges out the record for the #1 spot — Pollard and Ridley are finally producing.
teams.blurb: I almost put this team in the top spot this week, but decided against it, because the point differential between the two top teams isn't significant enough while the record is. Carmine's team has consistently been viewed as one of the biggest threats in the league, and with <mark class="hl-player">Tony Pollard</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Calvin Ridley</mark> finally producing, this team looks like it has the best starting lineup on paper by a large margin. If his team can consistently produce in the playoffs as it has in recent weeks, Carmine is primed for a championship run.

teams.synopsis: Back in the top three and dominant — sub-100 points only once all season, averaging 125+.
teams.blurb: Back into the top three this week, Charlie's team has been straight-up dominant. He's put up less than 100 points only once, and averages over 125 points a matchup (one of only three teams to do so). The return of <mark class="hl-player">Kyren Williams</mark> to this lineup did not disappoint, and if he keeps this up, Charlie looks like he'll be the winner of the 2023 PFFL Championship. Even though he plays two playoff-caliber teams to close the season, I see Charlie winning those weeks and finishing as a top seed in the AFC.

teams.synopsis: One of the few teams with zero holes in the starting lineup — playoffs are locked, seeding is the question.
teams.blurb: Brandon put up 122 points in Week 12, which may make you think he wouldn't fall in the rankings, but he only fell because another manager had a crazy week. Brandon has one of the few teams that genuinely doesn't have a hole in the starting lineup — both RBs are RB1s, all three starting WRs can have top-15 weeks, and the QB1 and TE1 provide good production. Playoffs aren't in question at this point, but seeding is. Brandon has an opportunity to overtake Carmine for the top spot in the AFC if he wins out and Carmine loses at least one more game.

teams.synopsis: A comfortable 5th spot with a lineup unchanged since Week 1 — a winning formula that doesn't need fixing.
teams.blurb: Cole's team remains a constant in the rankings this week, firmly securing the 5th spot. With a stable lineup that hasn't seen changes since Week 1, Cole seems to have found a winning formula. Despite lacking major alterations, Cole's team is poised for a historic PFFL Championship run, aiming for a breakthrough in franchise history. Bolstered by elite talent at WR and QB, Cole's success will hinge on the consistent overperformance of his RBs, TE, and flex players.

teams.synopsis: Out of the top five for the first time in six weeks, but a lock for the playoffs regardless.
teams.blurb: Aidan has fallen out of the top five for the first time in six weeks, but I still think this team is closer to the 5th-ranked team than the 7th. <mark class="hl-player">Dak Prescott</mark> has been one of the best players in fantasy this year, and when you pair him with the other top talents on this team, you have a squad that can beat anyone. This team is most likely a lock for the playoffs, but a tough schedule to finish the season — facing the 2nd- and 7th-ranked teams — will test them.

teams.synopsis: Produced playoff-caliber numbers in a loss — an easy closing matchup against Ben helps his odds a lot.
teams.blurb: He heard all the doubters. Baylen lost in Week 12, but his team showed out and produced 'playoff team' numbers, and if he wasn't trolling, maybe he would've won the week. Baylen's team doesn't have the best record for a playoff team, but an easy matchup against Ben to finish the season makes his odds of finishing .500 or better very likely. A few byes in the next two weeks may discourage this team a little, but nevertheless I believe them to be a playoff team.

teams.synopsis: One more win makes the playoffs very likely — though the Jefferson trade could still backfire.
teams.blurb: Staying within the top eight this week, Anthony's team had a down week, as <mark class="hl-player">Schultz</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Warren</mark> had bad games. This team is on the edge of not making the playoffs, but one more win makes his odds very likely. The trade for <mark class="hl-player">Jefferson</mark> was a big one, but if it ends up costing him a playoff spot, it might be viewed as one of the biggest backfires in PFFL history. I have full confidence this team finishes the season strong and makes the PFFL Playoffs for the 4th year in a row.

teams.synopsis: A tough draw with several key players on bye, but the record-vs-points math still leaves a path in.
teams.blurb: Once again, Max's team is ranked just outside the playoff picture. This team had the potential to be sneaky and fun, but a few poorly timed trades and some unlucky weeks have limited them. Not all hope is lost, though — if Max is able to finish with the same record as Anthony or Baylen, he'll most likely make the playoffs due to having more points scored than them. It'll be difficult with only two weeks left, but it's definitely possible. One wrench in those plans: Max has several key players on bye to finish the season, like <mark class="hl-player">Murray</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Robinson Jr.</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Moore</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Kincaid</mark>.

teams.synopsis: A loss leaves Deniz needing to win his next two just to have a shot at the playoffs.
teams.blurb: A loss in Week 12 leaves Deniz's team in a difficult situation — just like the managers below and above him, he'll now most likely have to win his next two games to have a chance at the playoffs. It's been an unfortunate 2023 season, with <mark class="hl-player">Achane</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Montgomery</mark> getting injured, <mark class="hl-player">Cooper</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Adams</mark> being underwhelming, and <mark class="hl-player">Pitts</mark> being Pitts. This team has been in the same position for most of the season, so it'd be characteristic to see it finish the year here.

teams.synopsis: A win keeps the playoff race alive, but he'll likely have to win out to make it happen.
teams.blurb: Ryan secured a win in Week 12, which keeps him in the playoff race, but he'll most likely have to win out to compete for a spot. After a strong 3-1 start to the season, Ryan lost six games in a row and was left in a hole, but back-to-back wins have him crawling out of it. Now, having only one bye week left for a starting player to finish out the season is crucial, but I wouldn't expect this manager to be done trading. Ryan lost in the championship last year, so expect him to do everything in his power to get back to the playoffs once again.

teams.synopsis: "Why is my team so ass, man" — a decade-long playoff streak may be about to end.
teams.blurb: "Why is my team so ass man," sad words to hear from the veteran manager. Andrew has made the playoffs every year since the beginning of the PFFL, but this year it looks like that streak may end. A big injury to his RB1 and TE1 left this team outmanned this season, but the pickup of Puka kept them in the playoff picture despite the odds. Even though he's not statistically eliminated, the loss to another 4-7 team in Week 12 basically shuts the door.

teams.synopsis: Playoff hopes are done, but a win over Quin all but locks up avoiding last place.
teams.blurb: Ben's playoff hopes may be done, but at least he practically secured not coming in last place this past week with a win over Quin. They're eliminated from the playoffs, and they've had some unfortunate losses this year — an easier schedule would've had this team in the playoff hunt, but that doesn't matter now. The past PFFL Champion will miss the playoffs for the second year in a row, but hopefully this ends next year.

teams.synopsis: Back to 14th after his biggest loss of the season — the Ohio punishment is now on the table.
teams.blurb: Back into the 14th spot for the first time in four weeks, Quin took the biggest loss of his season to Ben in Week 12. This loss most likely means Quin will have to complete the Ohio St. punishment, now that Ben has a better record and a lot more points scored. Quin's 2023 season is over, and hopefully he has better luck next year.
